source.title: Convergent Learning: Do different neural networks learn the same representations?
source.authors: Yi-Xuan Li; J. Yosinski; J. Clune; Hod Lipson; J. Hopcroft

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether independently initialized networks learn similar representations using neuron matching, mutual information, sparse prediction, and clustering; it is the study that introduces these measurements rather than a reproduction of an earlier method.
record.gate_note: The paper reports validation accuracies for four networks, but these are not representation-alignment outcomes. The cited studies and proposed future experiments are not results of this study. Rows record the paper's own alignment, prediction, and clustering results.
record.test_reason: This is one of the claim's two original sources and the origin of V3. It trains four AlexNet-style ImageNet networks from different seeds and measures unit matching, mutual information, sparse linear mapping and clustering. Because it is an original source, no verdicts are given.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is largely correct. It should add the fourth finding: mean activation distributions converge almost identically across networks, though per-unit magnitudes vary. It should also note that mutual information gave the same results as correlation, and that layers conv1–conv2 are the most convergent and conv4 the least.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures same-layer activation correlations and mutual information, matches or clusters units, and fits sparse linear prediction mappings between networks. It does not test scale, cross-modal alignment, or different architectures.
record.method_sensitivity: Alignment varies by layer: conv1 and conv5 have the strongest one-to-one matches, while intermediate layers are weaker. The authors report qualitatively similar matching results for correlation and mutual information.
record.problems: Four networks were trained, but the detailed pairwise alignment examples primarily use Net1 and Net2. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Some alignment results are shown only in figures. The sparse mapping results for conv3–conv5 are described as poor or inconclusive, and only one dataset and one architecture family are used.

untested.parts: All of it: there is no scale, capability, architecture, objective or data variation.
All of it: there are no vision-language models or paired captions.
Stitching with downstream performance, relative representations, unpaired mapping, and cross-architecture mapping.
Recurrence across different architectures or training regimes; SAE features and circuits.
Variation in neighbour count, input distribution, or out-of-distribution data.
The plateau, and the causes of alignment.

missing.what: Per-layer best and worst semi-matching correlations for the eight best and eight worst pairs (best near 0.96–1.00, worst 0.18–0.40 for conv1–conv3).
The distribution of mean unit activations converges across all four networks, but the unit ordering differs (e.g. the most active conv2 filter ranges from 49 to 120).
HAC clustering on the conv1 sparse mapping shows most leaf clusters pairing one Net1 unit with one Net2 unit, plus shared four-unit subspaces.
Between-net versus within-net cluster similarity distributions for conv1–conv5.

record.verdict_notes: This is an original source for V3, so no verdict labels are given. Only the Net1 vs Net2 pair is analysed in detail; all four networks appear only in the activation statistics. The rows' V4 links on the matching-count rows overstate the evidence, since those rows measure single-unit correspondence, not mapping loss.

versions.untested_parts: No scaling sweep, capability comparison across model sizes, or comparison of different architectures, objectives, datasets, or modalities.
No vision-language models or paired images and captions.

Only four independently initialized networks with the same AlexNet-derived architecture and ImageNet training setup; the detailed pairwise alignment results primarily compare Net1 and Net2. It does not compare all seeds or test individual units across training stages.
Tests linear sparse mappings on conv1–conv5 and feature matching/clustering, but not stitching layers, relative representations, or mapping without paired inputs.
Tests recurring visual features in neurons and clusters, not circuits or SAE features, and does not establish recurrence across different architectures or training regimes.
Compares correlation with mutual information, but does not vary neighbour count, other similarity settings, or input distributions; the principal results use ImageNet validation data.
No test separating shared data or objectives from a shared model of reality, nor a quantified plateau or degree of complete alignment.
